A strangely familiar brass lantern is lying on the ground.

Narrow Tunnel

You are standing at the southern end of a narrow tunnel where it opens into a wide cavern. The cavern is dimly illuminated by phosphorescent mosses clinging to its high ceiling. A deep ravine winds through the cavern, with a small stream at the bottom. The walls of the ravine are steep and crumbly. A foot bridge crosses the ravine to the south.
The lamp is now on.
Foot Bridge
You are standing on a crude but sturdy wooden foot bridge crossing a deep ravine. The path runs north and south from here.

expect.words: A strange little man in a long cloak appears suddenly in the room. He is wearing a high pointed hat embroidered with astrological signs. He has a long, stringy, and unkempt beard.

The Wizard draws forth his wand and waves it in your direction. It begins to glow with a faint blue glow. He peers at you from under his bushy eyebrows, as though you were not at all what he had been expecting, and had turned up anyway.

His eye goes to your hands, which hold nothing he values, and he relaxes a little: whatever you have come for, you have not found it yet. It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question, and the rest further in, past a room that will not keep still, which you will hear before you see it.
The Wizard, in a deep and resonant voice, speaks the word "Fumble!" He then vanishes, cackling gleefully.
Ooops! You dropped the lamp.
Taken.
Great Cavern

This is the center of the great cavern, carved out of the limestone. Stalactites and stalagmites of many sizes are everywhere. The room glows with dim light provided by phosphorescent moss, and weird shadows move all around you. A narrow path winds southwest among the stalagmites, and another leads northeast.
Shallow Ford

You are at the southern edge of a great cavern. To the south across a shallow ford is a dark tunnel which looks like it was once enlarged and smoothed. To the north a narrow path winds among stalagmites. Dim light illuminates the cavern.
Dark Tunnel

This is a dark tunnel with dim light to the northeast. The tunnel is smooth but dusty and filled with twigs and leaves, debris which becomes deeper as the tunnel branches into a wide corridor leading southwest and a narrower one leading southeast.

A faint whirring sound can be heard in that direction, as of something very large going round that will not keep still. On the east is a ruined archway choked with vegetation.
Formal Garden

This is the middle part of a formal garden. Hedges hide the cavern walls and a dim illumination comes from mosses far above. The path is of small crushed white stones. It winds among bushes and flower beds from south to north. To the north a small structure can be seen. To the south are peculiarly shaped bushes. There is a small gap in the hedges to the west.

This is the northern end of a formal garden. Hedges hide the cavern walls, and if you don't look up, the illusion is of a cloudy day outside. expect.words: ** U.S. News and Dungeon Report **
FAMED ADVENTURER TO EXPLORE GREAT UNDERGROUND EMPIRE

Our correspondents report that a world-famous and battle-hardened adventurer has been seen in the vicinity of the Great Underground Empire. Local grues have been reported sharpening their (slavering) fangs....
WIZARD STILL AT LARGE

The Wizard of Frobozz, dismissed from the court of Lord Dimwit Flathead for turning the royal mountain into a very large pile of gravel, is believed to have retired to the caverns south of the ravine, taking with him a quantity of the Empire's loose property (a pearl necklace, a Stradivarius and a crystal sphere are mentioned in the inventory, and the Bank of Zork has declined to comment on the rest). Visitors report a loud whirring from somewhere past the garden, as of a room that will not keep still, and nobody who has walked into it has come out the way they expected. He is described as doddering, petulant and armed with a wand, and the public is advised not to let him finish a word.

Topiary

This is the southern end of a formal garden. Hedges hide the cavern walls and mosses provide dim illumination. Fantastically shaped hedges and bushes are arrayed with geometric precision. They have not recently been clipped, but you can discern creatures in the shapes of the bushes: There is a dragon, a unicorn, a great serpent, a huge misshapen dog, and several human figures. On the west side of the garden the path leads through a rose arbor into a tunnel.
Carousel Room
You are in a large circular room whose high ceiling is lost in gloom. Eight identical passages leave the room.
A loud whirring sound comes from all around, and you feel sort of disoriented in here.

The disorientation is not all in your head. The floor, if you stand still on it a moment, is turning, slowly, and the eight passages go round with it, so that the one you came in by is already somewhere else. They all lead somewhere, every one of them; it is only a question of which, and the only way to settle that is to pick one and walk into it. The one that climbs a little, when it comes round, has a draught down it that smells of old brick and older water, and once, faintly, from up that way, you hear the grinding of a very heavy stone door.

expect.words: (take the passage)
A passage is not a thing to be picked up; it is a way, and the way to take it is to walk into it. Say which.

There is no up to it: the passage that climbs is one of the eight, and it goes round with the floor like the rest, so the only way into it is to pick a passage and walk. If the floor obliges, it climbs.
You're not sure which direction is which. This room is very disorienting.

That was the floor's doing and not yours: it turned while you were choosing, and the passage you chose went round with it, and the whirring is whatever turns it. A thing that is turned can presumably be stopped, by somebody who finds the works; and the works are not in that room so much as under it and off to one side, by the sound, which is loudest low down and toward the passage that climbs, as though the machinery were somewhere past the well at the end of that way.

This is a large room which was evidently used once as a quarry. Many large limestone chunks lie helter-skelter around the room. Some are rough-hewn and unworked, others smooth and well-finished. expect.words: Guarded Room

This room is cobwebby and musty, but tracks in the dust show that it has seen visitors recently. At the south end of the room is a stained and battered (but very strong-looking) door. To the north, a corridor exits. Imbedded in the door is a nasty-looking lizard head, with sharp teeth and beady eyes. The eyes move to watch you approach.
The lizard comes to life and snaps at you as you reach for the handle.
I've known strange people, but fighting a lizard?
The guardian seems impervious to your attack. In fact, your blows don't even seem to be landing.

The lizard wolfs down the china teapot, crunching greedily, and looks at you afterward with its tongue going, exactly as hungry as before. That was not what it wanted; it ate it because it was there, and it will not be giving it back.

expect.words: A lizard head the size of your own, imbedded in the door at about the height of a knocker, green, scaled, with a great many sharp teeth and two beady eyes that move to follow you. It is not carved. It is a lizard, and it is hungry, and the door is its. Its tongue flicks at the air the way a lizard's does when there are insects about: what it is hungry for is the kind of thing lizards eat, something that had legs and crunches, and a great deal of it. Anything else put in its mouth it will swallow out of habit, and not give back, and go on being hungry.
You can't see any such thing.
You're not in anything, unless you count the Wizard's domain, and there is no getting out of that.
